description:
FILED s466bc (Opus) from the #1037 probes.  PRE-EXISTING -- nothing in #1037
touches this path (the ruled-refusal classifier is only consulted where a
statement was ALREADY dropped, and this statement is never dropped).

REPRO (scratch/s466bc/p6.pl):

    no warnings;
    print "before\n";
    format STDOUT =
    \@<<<
    "x"
    .
    print "after\n";

PCL prints `before` and `after` and says NOTHING.  The emitted CL contains
(p-print "before") and (p-print "after") and no trace of the format at all --
no `;; PARSE ERROR:`, no drop announcement, no refusal.  perl 5.40.3 runs the
same program printing `before` / `after` too, so the OUTPUT happens to agree
here; what is lost is the format DEFINITION, which a later `write` would need
(`write` is already a no-op stub, docs/not-supported.md \xc2\xa7format / write).

WHAT PPI DOES (measured, PPI 1.291):

    PPI::Statement::Include   no warnings;
    PPI::Statement            print "b\n";
    PPI::Statement            format STDOUT =\n\@<<<\n"x"\n.\nprint "a\n";

i.e. ONE Statement from `format` to EOF -- PPI does not honour the `.`
terminator.  docs/not-supported.md's \xa7format entry already documents this and
says the source-level stripper (`_preprocess_source`) exists to defuse it;
what the entry does NOT say is that the stripper's SUCCESS path is silent.
The entry's "a header the stripper does not match ... refuses" half works and
is guarded (Pl/t/ruled-refusal-01.t exercises the classifier arm directly).

WHY IT MATTERS: this is a #138-family silence in the one place the project has
already decided must be loud.  Either the stripper announces what it removed
(the cheapest fix, and the same shape as the drop announcement), or the
statement is routed to the drop site so the existing `format/write` ruled
refusal fires and it becomes a statement-level die like every other refusal
(#1037).  The second is the consistent answer.

NOT DONE HERE because #1037's scope was the refusals that DIE at transpile
time; this one never reaches a refusal at all.  Sized: one announcement at the
stripper, or one routing change plus the not-supported entry's rewrite.
Guard would go in Pl/t/refusal-site-01.t, whose header already records the
gap and why the file does not cover it.
subject: A `format NAME = ... .` block that the source stripper DOES match still loses the format SILENTLY -- PPI swallows the picture lines AND every following statement into one Statement, and PCL emits the trailing statements with the format part simply gone
